lessons.title: Welcome to the Club
lessons.html:
You finished six weeks. You wrote who God has called you to be, cut your life down to three commitments, built a floor under each one, and reported your number to other men. That is not nothing. Most men never get that far.

The Club exists for one reason: so the plan you built keeps running after the cohort ends. The cohort built the system. The Club keeps the Ledger going and keeps you around brothers who will ask.

What your membership includes

  • The four steps, for reference. The Calling, The Commitments, The Floor and The Ledger, with the worksheet and the printable scorecard. Come back to them whenever a week falls apart.
  • A monthly reset. One short lesson every 30 days, six in all, each ending in one thing to do that week. Pay yearly and all six are open today.
  • The monthly live call. One hour on Google Meet, the second Tuesday of every month, 7 to 8 PM Central.
  • An accountability partner. Optional. A different member each month, and you trade scorecards on Sunday night.

How to use it

Do not try to read everything. Read Your weekly rhythm next, print the Ledger, and put Sunday's review on your calendar with a time. That is the whole job this week.

Be The Man is a faith-based coaching and consistency system, not medical treatment, diagnosis, or clinical therapy for ADHD.

lessons.title: Your weekly rhythm
lessons.html:
A system that only runs when you feel like it is a mood. This is the rhythm that keeps it a system. It takes about 20 minutes a week.

Sunday night: the Ledger (15 minutes)

  • Mark each day for each commitment: kept, floor, missed or not scheduled.
  • Write the number: for example, 13 of 15 kept. A floor day counts as kept.
  • Name the one miss that keeps coming back, in one line.
  • Write one change for Monday: smaller, earlier or clearer.
  • Send your number to your partner or post it on the call. A number nobody sees is easy to round up.

Monday morning: lock it (2 minutes)

Read your sentence. Check that every commitment still has a day, a time and a place this week. If the week is already crowded, decide now which ones run on the floor.

Wednesday: the floor check (1 minute)

Midweek is where plans quietly die. Ask one question: is anything slipping? If yes, drop to the bad-day version on purpose instead of letting it go to zero.

Second Tuesday: the call

Bring your last four scorecards and one miss you want help with. See the call lesson.

"Let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together" (Hebrews 10:24-25).

lessons.title: Step 1: The Calling
lessons.html:
Everything else answers to this page. When a commitment stops making sense, the problem is usually that you forgot why it is there.

What it is

One sentence on who God has called you to be, built from your roles: son of God, husband or future husband, father or future father, son, worker, brother. For each role you asked what God expects of you there, and what faithful looks like on a Tuesday.

"Write the vision; make it plain on tablets, so he may run who reads it" (Habakkuk 2:2).

Use it now

  • Read your sentence every day at the place and time you chose. If you no longer see it, move it to where your eyes already go.
  • Every 90 days, rewrite it. Seasons change. A new job, a new baby, a move: your roles shift, so the sentence should too.
  • If you lost it, do the worksheet again. It takes 20 minutes, or four 5-minute pieces.

lessons.title: Step 2: The Commitments
lessons.html:
Your sentence becomes no more than three commitments you can check each week. Three is not a lack of ambition. It is how a plan survives a real week.

"Let what you say be simply 'Yes' or 'No'" (Matthew 5:37).

The rules

  • Three at most. If you add one, retire one.
  • Checkable. Each one is a yes or no with a number. "Be more present" is not checkable. "Phone in the drawer, 7:40 to 9 PM, four nights" is.
  • Answer to the sentence. Ask of each one: does this move me toward the man in my sentence, or is it something I feel I should want?
  • Define the miss first. Decide before Monday what counts as a miss, so Sunday is counting, not arguing.

Use it now

Write your three on this week's Ledger. If one has been missed three weeks running, it is not a character problem. It is too big, too vague or at the wrong time. Take it to Step 3.

lessons.title: Step 3: The Floor
lessons.html:
The Floor is what keeps one bad Wednesday from ending the plan. It has two parts: a trigger, and a bad-day version.

"For the righteous falls seven times and rises again" (Proverbs 24:16).

Part 1: give it an address

Name what usually breaks each commitment: time slipping, evening fatigue, the phone, a crowded house, shame after a miss. Then lock the commitment to a day, a time, a place and a trigger. "Thursday, 7:40 PM, phone in the kitchen drawer." "After I park at home, before I go in, I pray for one minute." "This week" is not a time.

Part 2: build the floor

For each commitment, write the two-minute version you will still do on your worst day. Prayer becomes one verse and one sentence. Training becomes ten push-ups. Being present becomes five minutes of real attention when you walk in. A floor day counts as kept. That is the point.

Use it now

  • Every commitment on your Ledger has a written floor.
  • Your most-missed commitment gets a new trigger this week: earlier, or attached to something you already do.
  • When you feel the week slipping, drop to the floor on purpose. Zero is the only real miss.

lessons.title: Step 4: The Ledger
lessons.html:
The Ledger is how you find out what is true. Not how you feel about the week. What happened.

"One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much" (Luke 16:10). "Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another" (Proverbs 27:17).

How to score

  • Mark each day: ✓ kept, F floor (counts as kept), ✗ missed, – not scheduled.
  • Add it up as a number: 13 of 15, not "pretty good." Four out of seven is four out of seven.
  • Report it. Your partner, the call, or a brother you trust. The number goes to someone every week.
  • Take grace without shame. Write one honest, kind sentence to yourself, then one change for Monday.
  • Reset. No starting over next month, no making up lost days. Monday is a new week.

Use it now

Print the Ledger below, or copy it into a notebook. Put Sunday's review on your calendar with a time and a reminder.

lessons.title: Month 1: keep the Ledger alive
lessons.html:
The first month after a cohort is when most plans fade. Nobody is checking on Thursday anymore. This month has one job: keep the Sunday Ledger going four weeks in a row.

This month

  • Put the Sunday review on your calendar with a time and a reminder, every week.
  • Opt in for a partner in the call lesson, and send your number every Sunday.
  • If you miss a Sunday, do it Monday. A late Ledger is still a Ledger.

At the end of the month, write your four numbers in a row. That line is the first real evidence of who you are becoming.

lessons.title: Month 2: re-read your Calling
lessons.html:
By now your sentence may have gone quiet. You stopped seeing it. That is normal, and it is the moment to bring it back.

"So teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom" (Psalm 90:12).

This month

  • Read your sentence out loud once, this week, to someone in your house or to your partner.
  • Ask: is anything in it no longer true, or missing? Rewrite it if so.
  • Move it somewhere new: a new lock screen, a new spot on the mirror. A new place gets seen again.

lessons.title: Month 3: the 90-day commitment review
lessons.html:
Ninety days is long enough to know which commitments are working. This month you keep, retire or replace each one.

"The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance" (Proverbs 21:5).

This month

  • Lay out your last twelve Ledgers. For each commitment, count the kept weeks.
  • Keep the ones that are running. Consider raising the floor slightly.
  • Retire the ones that have become habit and no longer need tracking. Celebrate them.
  • Replace the ones that keep failing with something smaller, or at a better time. Never more than three.

lessons.title: Month 4: rebuild the Floor for a hard season
lessons.html:
Holidays, travel, a sick child, a new job. Hard seasons do not ask permission. A plan that only works in normal weeks is not finished.

This month

  • Name the next hard season on your calendar.
  • For each commitment, write a season floor: what still happens on the road, at a relative's house, or on four hours of sleep.
  • Tell your partner which weeks will run on the floor, before they come.

"His mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning" (Lamentations 3:22-23).

lessons.title: Month 5: bring the Ledger home
lessons.html:
The people you live with see your week more clearly than you do. This month you let them in on the plan.

This month

  • Tell the people in your house your sentence and your three commitments.
  • Ask one of them: "What would you notice if I kept these?" Write the answer down.
  • Pick one commitment where their answer is different from yours, and adjust it.

"Be doers of the word, and not hearers only" (James 1:22).

lessons.title: Month 6: become someone's brother
lessons.html:
You have kept a Ledger for six months. Now the most useful thing you can do is help another man start his.

"Two are better than one... For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow" (Ecclesiastes 4:9-10).

This month

  • Offer to take the hot seat on the next call, and walk the men through one thing you rebuilt.
  • Name one man outside the Club who keeps starting strong and stalling. Send him Step 1: bethemansystem.com/step-1.
  • Write down your six monthly numbers in a row and keep them where you will see them.

lessons.title: The monthly live call and your accountability partner
lessons.html:
The steps tell you what to do and when. The call and your partner make sure someone notices whether you did it.

The monthly live call

When: the second Tuesday of every month, 7:00 to 8:00 PM Central, starting February 9, 2027.

Where: Google Meet, at meet.google.com/pzg-pjvw-yvu. It's the same link every month. Keep it inside the Club.

What happens: one hour with Brian and the other members. Each man who wants to says his number for the month and the one miss that keeps coming back. Then we work on the misses. Nobody is made to talk, and the call is not recorded.

Before each call

  • Have your last four Ledgers in front of you
  • Count your kept days as a number, for example 51 of 60
  • Pick the one miss you want help with and write it in one line
  • Join two minutes early from a quiet room

Your accountability partner

Opt in once with the button below. On the first of each month you'll get an email introducing you to one other member. He is your partner for that month.

Every Sunday night, send him a photo of your Ledger, and he sends you his. Your reply only needs one line: "Got it. What's the plan for the misses?" If he hasn't sent his by Monday morning, ask for it. That question is the whole job.

To stop, reply "stop pairs" to any Club email.

How to know it's working

At the end of each month, compare your kept days with the month before. If the number went up, or the same miss showed up less often, it's working. If it didn't, bring that number to the next call. That's exactly what the call is for.
